Question 4 [12 marks]: How significant was the Nazi party to the collapse of the Weimar Republic? Integrate evidence from Source D and ONE other source from the Source Booklet in your answer.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 12):
10–12 marks: Provides a well-developed explanation of the significance of the Nazi party to the collapse of the Weimar Republic | Effectively integrates evidence from Source D and one other source to support response | Presents a well-structured, logical and cohesive response using appropriate historical terms and concepts
7–9 marks: Provides an explanation of the significance of the Nazi party to the collapse of the Weimar Republic | Integrates evidence from Source D and one other source to support response | Presents a structured response using appropriate historical terms and concepts
4–6 marks: Describes some reasons for the significance of the Nazi party and/or the collapse of the Weimar Republic | Makes some reference to the sources and relevant historical knowledge | Communicates using some historical terms and concepts
1–3 marks: Makes a general statement(s) in relation to the question | May use some historical terms and/or concepts

Significance of the Nazi party:
• Manipulation of the political context of ‘Dolschstosslegende’ (stab in the back legend) and anti-Treaty of Versailles sentiment (Source A)
• Nazi’s use of propaganda including Hitler’s cult of personality
• Popular support (Source D)
• Nazi appeal to the workers (Source C)
• Nazi rhetoric blaming Jews/big business for the plight of the worker (Source C)
• Introduction of laws such as the Reichstag Fire Decree (to remove civil liberties), Enabling Act (to bypass the Reichstag) or banning political parties (Source D).

• Economic factors (Sources A and B)

– Germany’s debt and reliance on the Dawes Plan (Source B)
– Had been ‘financially disarmed’ as well as militarily disarmed (Source B).
